evidence: A missing read-only gate on write-capable `undo()`/`redo()` against a test-helper dependency. A permission defect and an API-brittleness one.

panel.summary: Write-capable undo()/redo() have no read-only/permission gate; the read-only check lives only in the two view-level callers
panel.evidence: `YorkieNoteStore.undo()` (yorkie-note-store.ts:93) calls `doc.history.undo()`, which mutates the shared CRDT, and neither the store nor `NoteEditorAPI.undo()` (packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:431) consults `readOnly`. The only things stopping a viewer-role share session from writing are two view-level gates: the history keymap is replaced by `[]` when `readOnly` (editor.ts:213) and the vim route checks `EditorView.editable` (editor.ts:52), plus the toolbar hiding the buttons behind `canFormat = !readOnly && mode !== 'view'` (notes-toolbar.tsx:200). Attack chain: a viewer opens a shared note (shared-document.tsx:288 sets `readOnly = resolved.role === 'viewer'`, line 310 mounts NotesView with it) and any caller reaching `api.undo()` — a future toolbar/menu/shortcut wired without re-checking readOnly, or a keymap switch to vim on a mount whose editable facet changes — writes reverse ops into the document. Server-side the Yorkie auth webhook would reject an `rw` PushPull, but only once `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE === 'true'`; the default is shadow mode, which logs and allows (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:97-105), so such a write persists. I found no currently reachable caller, hence low confidence; the gap is that the enforcement point is not on the operation that writes. Existing stores (yorkie-slides-store.ts:632, yorkie-doc-store.ts) share this shape, so it is a pattern-level gap rather than a new one.
panel.finding_key: packages/frontend/src/app/notes/yorkie-note-store.ts::write-capable undo()/redo() have no read-only/permission gate; the read-only check lives only in the two view-level callers

coderabbit.detail: **Avoid depending on `doc.getUndoStackForTest()` outside tests.** `Document.getUndoStackForTest()` is exposed in `@yorkie-js/sdk` 0.7.13, but its `ForTest` suffix indicates it is a test helper, not the stable public history API. Keeping the store’s `undoFloor` calculation tied to this helper makes application code brittle to future SDK changes.
